concept.name: Currency carry trade
concept.definition: A strategy of borrowing (funding) in a low-interest-rate currency and investing in a high-interest-rate currency without hedging the exchange-rate exposure, aiming to earn the interest rate differential. Its profitability violates uncovered interest parity, and research documents that carry-trade returns are negatively skewed — subject to sudden crash risk when funding liquidity falls and positions unwind en masse.
concept.intuition: Collect the interest-rate gap between two currencies and hope the exchange rate doesn't move against you before you exit.
concept.mechanics: The trader shorts the funding currency (e.g. a low-yielder) and goes long the investment currency, earning the rate differential as 'carry' plus or minus any exchange-rate change. Because UIP predicts the high-rate currency should depreciate by the differential, persistent carry profits are a pricing anomaly; unwind episodes cluster when risk appetite and funding liquidity decline, producing negatively skewed, crash-prone returns and excess co-movement among currencies with similar interest rates.
concept.formula: Approximate carry-trade return = (r_invest - r_funding) + percentage change in the exchange rate (investment currency vs funding currency) over the holding period.
concept.failure_modes: Carry trades crash during liquidity squeezes and risk-off episodes: sudden unwinding produces large depreciations of high-yield currencies (negative skewness), e.g. 2008. Losses can exceed years of accumulated carry, and funding-liquidity constraints force deleveraging exactly when prices gap.
concept.misconceptions: The interest differential is not a free lunch: it is compensation for crash risk, not a market inefficiency that can be harvested risklessly; carry strategies are not reliably profitable on a risk-adjusted basis.
concept.example: Borrowing Japanese yen at a near-zero rate to buy Australian dollars yielding several percent more earns the differential while AUD/JPY is stable, but a sharp yen rally during a global risk-off episode can wipe out the position.

citations.source: NBER Working Paper 14473 — Carry Trades and Currency Crashes (Brunnermeier, Nagel, Pedersen)
